## Beachhead in Idaho and Utah; a market of about $307M a year across six countries {#market}

<span class="kicker">Market · estimates unless marked</span>

<figure class="rings" aria-label="Three market rings, not to scale">
<div class="ring ring--outer"><b>~0.9M</b> small businesses on Stripe <em>estimate</em></div>
<div class="ring ring--tam"><b>TAM ~426,000</b> organizations big enough to pay · ~$307M a year; schools, co-ops, churches ~$156M <em>estimate</em></div>
<div class="ring ring--sam"><b>SAM ~77,000</b> on their own Stripe · ~$55M a year <em>estimate</em></div>
<div class="ring ring--som"><b>SOM ~1,200</b> paying · ~$0.86M ARR, year 3 <em>estimate</em></div>
</figure>

<p class="fine">Launch order: US, ESA states first, starting with Idaho and Utah microschools → Canada without Quebec → UK → Australia and New Zealand → Ireland.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/market-research.md` §6 (researched 2026-11-07; summarized in `docs/business/business-plan.md` §8, "Market size (estimates)", in docs PR #38): §6.1 the three rings (outer ring about 0.9M small businesses on Stripe in six countries, from BuiltWith counts of live Stripe sites: ~695,000–710,000 US and ~82,000–86,000 UK sourced, the rest estimated at the UK rate; websites aren't businesses); §6.7 TAM, SAM, SOM (TAM = paid-eligible organizations × $720 a year at the realized $60 a month: 426,000 total, 217,000 in the focus verticals, ~$307M / ~$156M; SAM = those billing through a Stripe account they control: 77,000, ~$55M; SOM = a 3-year share: ~1,200 customers, ~$0.86M ARR, ~$0.81M net of affiliates; sensitivity $45 to $76.50 a month gives TAM $230–391M and SOM ~$0.65–1.1M); §6.9 launch order (US nationally, ESA states first: AZ, FL, TX, UT, ID, then AR, IA, TN, AL, WV; Canada without Quebec; UK; Australia then New Zealand; Ireland with an EU plan). All four rings are estimates. The rings overlap rather than nest (focus organizations without Stripe are in the TAM, not the outer ring); the bars are not to scale. The SOM fits the plan's 1,000–1,300 paying by year 3 (`docs/business/financial-model.md` §5).

Owner decision, 2026-11-07: the market is the US and each English-speaking country; Idaho and Utah microschools are the first beachhead (`docs/business/business-plan.md` §1 still says "the working default"). Utah's program is not named while its appeal is pending.
:::

## No accounting product hands the payer a receipt anyone can check {#competition}

<span class="kicker">Competition · list prices a month</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card"><h3>General accounting</h3><p>QuickBooks $38–340, user caps on every plan. Xero $27–97. Trifold replaces or feeds them.</p></div>
<div class="card card--green"><h3>AI-native accounting</h3><p>Puzzle $30–360. Digits $65–250. Same buyers; no payer receipts.</p></div>
<div class="card card--ink"><h3>Bookkeeping services</h3><p>Pilot from $99; human-led $349–849+. Trifold sells this through partners.</p></div>
<div class="card card--quiet"><h3>Vertical software</h3><p>Jackrabbit $49–245. Pike13 $139–249. Partners: they run operations, Trifold keeps the books.</p></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/market-research.md` §1 (the four groups and where Trifold fits), §2 (QuickBooks $38 / $85 / $140 / $340 with user caps 1 / 3 / 5 / 25; Xero $27 / $59 / $97; Puzzle $30 / $72 / $120 / $360 on its own page, 2026-11-06; Digits $65 / $100 / ~$250; Pilot Bookkeeping Essentials $99 on Pilot's page, aggregators $199 and human-led $349–849+; Jackrabbit $49–245; Pike13 $139–249) and §3 point 5 ("Nobody offers provable books"). Where vendor pages and aggregators differ, the vendor page wins (market-research header). Recheck before quoting.

Nearest competitor: Airtight (Australia and the Gulf) signs entries with Ed25519 inside its own system; Trifold gives the signed receipt to the person who paid, with a free checker and an open format; Airtight has no free tier (`docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §9, reviewed from its own pages, claims unverified).
:::

## List prices give $76.50 a month per organization; about $60 after discounts {#arpu}

<span class="kicker">Revenue per paying organization · illustrative</span>

<figure class="stack">
<div class="stack-bar" role="img" aria-label="Assumed list-price mix: Starter 40 percent at $29, Pro 35 percent at $79, Audited 20 percent at $149, bookkeeper bundle 5 percent counted at $149.">
<div class="seg-a" style="width: 40%">Starter 40%<small>$29 → $11.60</small></div>
<div class="seg-b" style="width: 35%">Pro 35%<small>$79 → $27.65</small></div>
<div class="seg-c" style="width: 20%">Audited 20%<small>$149 → $29.80</small></div>
<div class="seg-d" style="width: 5%">5%</div>
</div>
<figcaption>The last 5% is the bookkeeper bundle, counting only Trifold's $149 share ($7.45).</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--ink"><span class="big">$76.50</span><p>List-price mix: the upside case</p></div>
<div class="card card--green"><span class="big">≈ $60</span><p>Realized base case. By year: ≈ $40 (Starter and the compliance pack only), ≈ $55, ≈ $65</p></div>
</div>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> $76.50 × 0.80 (about 40% non-profits at half price) × 0.975 (annual billing).</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/business-plan.md` §8 as updated in docs PR #38 (2026-11-07): list-price mix 40% Starter, 35% Pro, 20% Audited, 5% bundle counting only Trifold's ~$149 share = $11.60 + $27.65 + $29.80 + $7.45 = $76.50 (the upside case; credit packs left out); realized base case $76.50 × 0.80 × 0.975 ≈ $59.70 (about 40% non-profits or co-ops at about half price; about 15% annual with two months free); by year ~$40 (year 1: Starter with the compliance pack only, Pro waits for its features), ~$55 (Pro arrives, Audited late), ~$65 (the full mix plus packs). Unit economics: `docs/business/financial-model.md` §7 (#38).

Every number is an assumption: no price tests have run (`docs/business/market-research.md` §5; experiment A in business-plan §11).
:::

## If 1,000 organizations pay by year 3, the run-rate is about $0.8–0.9M {#arr}

<span class="kicker">Annual run-rate at year end · illustrative</span>

<figure class="bars">
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Year 1 · 50</span><div class="track"><span class="fill fill--list" style="--w: 3.75%"></span><span class="fill" style="--w: 1.96%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 3.75%">$24K · list $46K</span></div></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Year 2 · 300</span><div class="track"><span class="fill fill--list" style="--w: 22.5%"></span><span class="fill" style="--w: 16.2%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 22.5%">$198K · list $275K</span></div></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Year 3 · 1,000</span><div class="track"><span class="fill fill--list" style="--w: 75%"></span><span class="fill" style="--w: 63.7%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 75%">$780K · list $918K</span></div></div>
<figcaption><span class="legend"><span><i></i>Base case</span><span><i class="list"></i>List-price upside</span></span>Paying organizations × that year's revenue each × 12. Base revenue in the year: ≈ $14K, $122K, $525K.</figcaption>
</figure>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> Counts and prices are assumptions, not forecasts. Platform and Witness API revenue left out.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/business-plan.md` §8 as updated in docs PR #38: paying organizations 50 / 300 / 1,000 at year end (free and self-hosted 300 / 2,000 / 8,000); base run-rate ARR (paying × that year's ARPU × 12) ~$24K / ~$198K / ~$780K; base revenue in the year ~$14K / ~$122K / ~$525K; upside (list price, full mix from day one) run-rate ~$46K / ~$275K / ~$918K, revenue in the year ~$28K / ~$170K / ~$618K; Platform and Witness API small in year 2, 10–20% on top in year 3. Growth (same section; `docs/business/financial-model.md` §5): 0.75% a month free-to-paid, 3% a month paid churn, plus about 4, 15 and 35 direct paid sign-ups a month in years 1–3; the free pool alone gives only about 10–20, 80–160 and 370–720 paying by the year-ends.

The SOM in `docs/business/market-research.md` §6.7 (~1,200 paying, ~$0.86M ARR in year 3) sits between the base and the upside. Bars on one linear scale ($918K = 75% of the track).
:::

<span class="kicker">One month in year 3 · illustrative</span>

<figure class="bars bars--zero">
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Net revenue</span><div class="track"><span class="fill" style="--from: 15%; --w: 49%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 64%">$65K</span></div></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Cost of revenue</span><div class="track"><span class="fill fill--clay" style="--from: 50.1%; --w: 13.9%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 64%">−$16.5–20.5K</span></div></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Gross profit</span><div class="track"><span class="fill fill--green" style="--from: 15%; --w: 35.1%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 50.1%">$45–49K · 69–75%</span></div></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Operating costs</span><div class="track"><span class="fill fill--clay" style="--from: 3.6%; --w: 46.5%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 50.1%">−$62K</span></div></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="label">Operating income</span><div class="track"><span class="fill fill--clay" style="--from: 3.75%; --w: 11.25%"></span><span class="value" style="--at: 15%">−$13–17K a month</span></div></div>
<figcaption>The line marks zero. Per paying organization, gross margin is 75–80% if support costs about $8 a month; about 70% at $12.</figcaption>
</figure>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> Hand arithmetic, not a model run. Includes founder pay.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/financial-model.md` §5, "What month 36 should roughly show", as updated in docs PR #38: gross collected ≈ $77,200 (1,000 paying × ~$64.70 realized incl. compliance packs; credit packs ≈ $2,500; bookkeeper passthrough ≈ $10,000); net revenue ≈ $65,400 (less the passthrough and ≈ $1,800 firm wholesale discounts); COGS ≈ $16,500–20,500 (Stripe ≈ $2,600; support $8,000–12,000; AI ≤ $4,700; witness ≈ $500; hosting under $1,000); gross margin ≈ 69–75% company-wide; opex ≈ $62,000 (marketing $25,000, three hires $28,800, founder pay $6,000, affiliate commissions ≈ $1,400, software and legal $800); operating income ≈ −$13,000 to −$17,000 a month. "Trifold isn't yet profitable at month 36. Break-even needs about 1,250–1,350 paying schools at this cost base, or marketing held near $8,000 a month, or the list-price case." Per-school gross margin 75–80% with support near $8, about 70% at $12: financial-model §7.

The deck's earlier "operating income positive by year 3" came from the pre-#38 model and is withdrawn. Bars on one linear scale: zero at 15% of the track, $1K = 0.75%.
:::

## The strongest moat, Trifold's countersignature, ships next; the license is the weakest {#moat}

<span class="kicker">Defensibility, strongest first</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><h3>1 · The witness</h3><p>Trifold's countersignature and public log. A fork can't copy it. <span class="tag tag--next">next</span></p></div>
<div class="card card--green"><h3>2 · The open standard</h3><p>The receipt format and checker (Apache-2.0) and test data (CC0).</p></div>
<div class="card card--ink"><h3>3 · The trademark</h3><p>Forks must rename. Unregistered; clearance search first.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--quiet"><h3>4 · Rifo on the books</h3><p>The assistant and workflows on top of the ledger. <span class="tag tag--next">next</span></p></div>
<div class="card card--quiet"><h3>5 · The license</h3><p>FSL blocks a hosted clone for two years per release; then Apache-2.0.</p></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/business-plan.md` §9 ("Moat, strongest first", in this order) and §5 ("The license is the weakest of the moats"). Status: the witness and Rifo are not built (business-plan §3; AGENTS.md "Claims"). Only the receipt and seal format, spec and verifier are Apache-2.0 and the vectors CC0; the KPI spec and event envelope are FSL (AGENTS.md "Licensing", open item 4). Trademark: `TRADEMARKS.md` (a draft; nothing registered, ™ only) and business-plan §10 (Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold; old TRIFOLD filings; search classes 9, 36, 42).

Licensing detail (AGENTS.md; business-plan §5; pricing-strategy §8): tfd is FSL-1.1-ALv2 from 0.10.0 (releases up to 0.9.0 stay Apache-2.0); each release becomes Apache-2.0 two years after it ships (the owner kept two years on 2026-11-07); FSL over BSL, Elastic and SSPL because it is short, fixed and converts. Say "source-available" or "free to self-host" for tfd. The hosted service, Rifo and the witness are proprietary.
:::

## Organizations and accounting firms first; partners once 20 pay {#gtm}

<span class="kicker">Go-to-market · three stages</span>

<div class="timeline">
<div class="stage stage--next"><span class="when">Stage A · months 0–6</span><h3>Founder-led, with firms</h3>
<ul><li>Schools, co-ops and churches</li><li>~5 firms as co-design partners</li><li>Networks and co-ops</li><li>Organizations refer organizations</li></ul></div>
<div class="stage stage--next"><span class="when">Stage B · months 6–12</span><h3>More firms</h3>
<ul><li>The Practice firm tier</li><li>More firms bringing clients</li></ul></div>
<div class="stage stage--later"><span class="when">Stage C · after ~20 paying</span><h3>Partners</h3>
<ul><li>Affiliates: 20% for 24 months</li><li>Practice Pro, after ~100 paying</li><li>Vertical software</li><li>Witness API, once the witness ships</li></ul></div>
</div>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> Cost to win a customer: referrals ~$130; firms ~$0 cash; affiliates $245–325; founder-led $300–500; paid ads $800–1,500, avoided.</p>

::: {.notes}
Cost to acquire a customer by channel: `docs/business/financial-model.md` §7 as updated in docs PR #38 (founder-led ~$300–500, LTV/CAC 3–5×; schools refer schools ~$130; affiliates ~$245–325 at the flat 20%, paid as earned; firms ~$0 cash, the cost is the Practice discount or wholesale margin; paid ads and content ~$800–1,500, avoid in years 1–2; LTV ~$1,500 at ~$45–48 contribution and 3% monthly churn).

Owner decision of 2026-11-07: accounting firms are a key enabler. Stage A: founder-led outreach to schools, co-ops and churches, about 5 accounting firms as co-design partners (Listed tier plus a written agreement), networks and co-ops, and organization-refers-organization credit; Stage B: the Practice tier and more firms; Stage C after about 20 paying: affiliates (one flat 20% of subscription revenue for 24 months), Practice Pro after about 100 paying clients, vertical software, the Witness API. The docs may be updated to match on the stacked docs branch.

It sequences what the docs list: `docs/business/business-plan.md` §7 (phases 0–3; growth loops; phase 1: ~10 CPA partners); `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §1 (channels), §2 (firm tiers: Listed at 1 client, Practice at 5, Practice Pro at 15), §3 (the 24-month cash limit, owner's decision), §3.2 (a month for a month, account credit, up to 12), §3.4 (networks and co-ops as one affiliate), §6 item 5 (which program ships first was open); `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §4c (free firm seats). The docs' affiliate tiers (25/30/35%) are replaced by the owner's flat 20%. The Witness API needs the witness (business-plan §3).
:::

## Three experiments in the next 90 days decide price, demand and cost {#experiments}

<span class="kicker">What we test before scaling</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><h3>Price</h3><p>Test the plans with 10–15 schools that aren't the founder's own.</p></div>
<div class="card card--green"><h3>Receipt demand</h3><p>Do families, CPAs and a program administrator want and use the receipt?</p></div>
<div class="card card--ink"><h3>Cost and reliability</h3><p>Run 2 schools for 60 days; measure cost, support and errors.</p></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Agreed in the 2026-11-07 deck review. They are experiments A, B and C in `docs/business/business-plan.md` §11 as updated in docs PR #38. They answer the gaps the docs name: `docs/business/market-research.md` §5 (no willingness-to-pay interviews; state program receipt rules need primary sources); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §8 ("What would change the outlook most": conversion, whether Rifo can close a month) and §11 item 5 (test prices with 5–10 design-partner schools); `docs/business/financial-model.md` §5 (AI cost per credit and hosting are assumptions to replace with measured cost).
:::

## Four risks, and how each is handled {#risks}

<span class="kicker">Risks</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>A big vendor hosts a clone</h3><p>FSL bars it for two years per release; the witness can't be cloned.</p></div>
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>Over-claiming</h3><p>We claim only what has shipped: signed receipts and sealed books.</p></div>
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>Tax preparation is regulated</h3><p>Trifold prepares books; licensed CPAs sign returns.</p></div>
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>Student data</h3><p>No names in receipts; privacy law checked per school type.</p></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/business-plan.md` §10 (the risk table; these four rows, shortened). Also there: what the witness promises (narrowly, "Trifold saw this exact record at time T"), key compromise, erasure that could break receipts (an owner decision before release, `packages/atm/ROADMAP.md` milestone 1), trademark conflict (Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold; clearance search), license backlash, deep competitor discounts. Pricing risks: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §10 (the top tier, now Audited, needs Rifo to close reliably).
:::
